title: CPU macro has no FP_PIN_ORDER_CFG - every regeneration reshuffles ~98% of boundary pins and can wreck SoC CTS
description:
MEASURED 2026-08-09 while chasing the GH #96 run-21 -> run-22 cpu_clk regression (-60.66 ps -> -596.00 ps, 690 violators).

ROOT CAUSE: pnr/asap7/cpu/config.json has NO FP_PIN_ORDER_CFG, so OpenROAD's io-placement step free-floats the CPU macro's boundary pins according to whatever internal placement that particular block run produced. Block-level placement is already known to be non-deterministic here (setup WS bounced +21.64 / +14.36 / +2.80 ps across three runs of near-identical RTL).

MEASURED CHURN between two consecutive macro regenerations (git HEAD LEF vs regenerated LEF, 401 pins compared): 393 pins MOVED, largest ~126 units inside a 130x130 um macro. Only clk_i stayed fixed at (6.078, 0.0); rst_n_i moved 31.728 -> 25.572. Ordinary data/control pins landed on effectively different edges.

CONSEQUENCE CHAIN (each step measured, not inferred):
  macro pin reshuffle
  -> SoC global placement perturbed around u_cpu
  -> TritonCTS builds a worse-balanced cpu_gated_clk_regs subtree; a NEW cell delaybuf_0_cpu_clk appears (0 occurrences in run 21's netlist, 1 in run 22); u_cpu_cg.u_icg CLK->GCLK goes 79.3 ps -> 285.1 ps (same cell type, so loading/placement, not library)
  -> post-CTS cpu_clk skew roughly DOUBLES: worst_hold -485.6 -> -922.1 ps, worst_setup -436.2 -> -865.2 ps (stage 32 or_metrics_out.json, the flow's own numbers)
  -> post-CTS hold violations 805 -> 4702 endpoints; resizer inserts 680 -> 4814 hold buffers; final HB4xp67 population 1934 -> 6017
  -> chained hold buffers (9+ deep on the worst path) consume the setup budget
  -> cpu_clk setup WNS -60.66 ps -> -596.00 ps, and sys_clk fell +83.79 -> +40.78 ps too.

REJECTED HYPOTHESIS (recorded so it is not re-tried): the RTL change that triggered the regeneration made apb_pready_o/apb_pslverr_o registered outputs, and the obvious theory was that their new fast clk->Q launch caused the hold explosion. Measured clk-to-Q delta is only ~9-14 ps (apb_pready_o cell_rise 247.9 -> 238.7 ps at min load) -- one to two orders of magnitude too small to explain a ~900 ps skew swing. The RTL change is merely what forced a regeneration; the instability is the bug.

ALSO REJECTED: the 25 ps real hold margin from bead s9f is not the amplifier -- raw pre-fix violations were already hundreds of ps (-332 ps in run 21, -782 ps in run 22) before any margin applies.

FIX: author an FP_PIN_ORDER_CFG for rv32i_cpu_top from a known-good layout (git HEAD's LEF is the run-21 macro that closed at -60.66 ps) and add it to pnr/asap7/cpu/config.json, so the boundary is stable across every future regeneration. LibreLane supports the variable (librelane/steps/openroad.py + steps/odb.py). Validate with one CPU block re-run (~40 min) by diffing the resulting LEF pin coordinates against the reference, then one SoC run.

WIDER IMPACT: this applies to the GPU macro too (pnr/asap7/gpu/config.json) and to any Sky130 macro flow. Any time a macro is regenerated for an unrelated reason, the integrating top can silently lose timing for reasons that have nothing to do with the change being made. That is exactly what happened here and it cost two SoC runs to see.
close_reason: FIXED. pnr/asap7/cpu/pin_order.cfg (401 signal pins) added and wired via FP_PIN_ORDER_CFG in pnr/asap7/cpu/config.json:150-151; rationale in pnr/asap7/cpu/README_pin_order.md (the file itself carries no comments -- LibreLane's ioplace parser treats any non-#N/#E/#S/#W '#' line as a pin identifier). Determinism PROVEN: two CPU block runs with the same config now produce a byte-identical LEF, 0/401 pins moved (was 393/401). That made tuning measurable for the first time -- block slack had previously drawn randomly from a ~47 ps band -- and run 23 then closed cpu_clk at +9.79 ps / 1282 MHz. Merged in PR #135 (f7868b1). The identical untreated exposure on the ASAP7 GPU macro (327 pins, no FP_PIN_ORDER_CFG) and on the Sky130 macros is tracked separately.

title: check_cdc_timing.tcl exceptions never bind on the flattened ASAP7 SoC netlist (slash vs dot, and cells are anonymous)
description:
GH #96 ran pnr/scripts/check_cdc_timing.tcl against a real routed netlist for the FIRST time (RUN_2026-08-06_09-44-51). Result: CDC-CHECK-RESULT: FAIL, 42 findings, of which 36 are CDC-EXCEPTION-MISS -- i.e. the exceptions in phase5_soc_multiclock_check.sdc matched EMPTY collections and were never applied. Breakdown of the 172 miss lines: sec.11 x30 (async_axi_fifo), sec.12 x16 + sec.12a x16 (apb_cdc_bridge u_apb_pll2_cdc / u_apb_dbg_cdc), sec.13 x10 (PMU/IRQ). By kind: 60 payload, 50 gray-pointer, 32 toggle, 25 single-bit, 25 mem_q.

GOOD NEWS FIRST: the checker did exactly what bead dwp designed it to do -- it refused to report PASS when its own patterns bound to nothing, and failed loudly. This is a bug in the PATTERNS, not evidence of a CDC timing violation. No CDC budget was measured either way, so the boundary is currently UNVERIFIED post-route.

ROOT CAUSE, measured on the routed netlist with OpenSTA:
  '*u_cpu_axi_cdc/u_aw_fifo/u_wr_ptr_to_rd*'  (slash, as written) -> 0 cells, 0 nets
  '*u_cpu_axi_cdc.u_aw_fifo.u_wr_ptr_to_rd*'  (dot)               -> 0 cells, 6 NETS
  '*u_cpu_axi_cdc.u_aw_fifo*'                                     -> 0 cells, 22 NETS
  '*u_apb_dbg_cdc*'                                               -> 0 cells, 13 NETS
Two independent problems:
 (1) SEPARATOR. SYNTH_HIERARCHY_MODE=flatten leaves hierarchical names joined by '.' as escaped identifiers (e.g. \u_cpu_axi_cdc.u_ar_fifo.rd_bin_q). The SDC was authored with '/' separators against RTL hierarchy. Same class as the known macro_placement.cfg dot-vs-slash trap.
 (2) OBJECT TYPE. After flatten the CELLS are anonymous (_419265_ etc): get_cells/get_pins match ZERO for every hierarchical pattern. Only get_nets matches. So exceptions must be expressed as -through [get_nets ...], not on pins/cells.

ALSO: some RTL signal names do not survive at all. 'mem_q' has 0 occurrences anywhere in the netlist (the unpacked flop array is fully renamed), and 'wr_gray_q' is gone while 'wr_gray_d' survives. So the 25 mem_q exceptions CANNOT be re-expressed by name; they need a different formulation (e.g. -from [all_registers -clock cpu_clk] -to [all_registers -clock sys_clk] scoped by -through on a surviving net, or constrain the surviving *_d nets).

FIX PLAN: (a) switch all patterns to dot separators; (b) retarget from pins/cells to get_nets with -through; (c) re-express the mem_q class without relying on that name; (d) add a binding assertion so a future pattern drift fails at authoring time, not after a 5 h run -- the existing CDC-EXCEPTION-MISS machinery already does this, it just needs to be exercised against a netlist in CI or a synth-only run rather than only at signoff.

Until fixed, the post-route CDC budget verification for the 2-domain SoC is NON-FUNCTIONAL.
close_reason: Closed

comments.author: RD-Chuanseng.Ng
comments.text:
FIXED and INDEPENDENTLY VERIFIED (2026-08-06). check_cdc_timing.tcl + phase5_soc_multiclock_check.sdc reworked (+539/-156 lines). Against RUN_2026-08-06_09-44-51: make check-cdc-timing-asap7-soc now exits 0 with CDC-EXCEPTION-MISS count 0 and CDC-CHECK-RESULT: PASS (re-run by me, not just reported by the implementer).

THREE root causes, not the two originally filed:
 (1) separator: hierarchy survives flatten only as literal '.' in escaped identifiers, not '/';
 (2) object class: cells are anonymous post-flatten so get_cells/get_pins name patterns always return empty - only get_nets can match;
 (3) NEW - OpenSTA's -filter "name =~ <pat>" mis-parses a literal '.' even between wildcards: '*u_aw_fifo.u_wr_ptr_to_rd*' -> 0 matches while '*.d_i*' -> 231,528 matches (i.e. nearly every net). Patterns must be '*'-joined chains of DOT-FREE substrings. This is why my original evidence (positional 'get_nets <pattern>' with dots, which DOES work and returned 6 nets) did not transfer to the -filter form used in the SDC. Both measurements were correct; the two APIs differ.

SEMANTIC FIX (confirmed against cdc_2ff_sync.sv/cdc_gray_fifo.sv): the old exceptions targeted u_*_ptr_to_*/q_o = sync_q[STAGES-1], which is entirely INSIDE the destination domain - a destination-only path, not a crossing. All exceptions re-pointed at the launch->first-capture segment (d_i where it survives, else the source register's own net, e.g. rd_gray_q where u_rd_ptr_to_wr.d_i collapsed into it).

PRECEDENCE (measured, and it corrected an initial wrong assumption): a -through exception is ALWAYS dominated by an overlapping -from/-to one regardless of order or specificity, so every per-crossing exception now uses -from/-to. Between two overlapping -from/-to exceptions precedence is pure DECLARATION ORDER (last wins), NOT specificity - proven by reversing the order. Hence the domain-wide fallback is declared BEFORE sections 11-13.
Two further silent-no-op bugs were found and fixed: one-hop -of_objects grabbed an intervening polarity inverter (ASAP7 DFFASRHQNx1 exposes only QN) instead of the real register, fixed with get_fanin/get_fanout -flat -only_cells; and synthesis-shared buffering put fanout on unrelated same-domain cells for one bus bit, fixed by intersecting against all_registers -clock <expected> and applying per-bit.

INVENTORY: 36 named exceptions (all missing) -> 19 name-matched crossing-specific + 2 domain-wide fallbacks covering the 17 that are unmatchable by name post-flatten (5 mem_q + 6 cmd_*/resp_* x 2 bridges). No crossing dropped.

BUDGET VERDICTS on the real routed netlist, all MET: gray-pointer wr2rd +275/+759 ps vs 390/875 budget; rd2wr +294/+779; apb_pll2 toggle +676/+1644 vs 780/1750; apb_dbg toggle +676/+1644; PMU/IRQ single-bit +645 vs 780; domain-wide fallback +174..+759 vs 702/875-1575.

NON-VACUITY PROVEN (my own negative controls, the thing that matters most here): forcing all 10 cdc_apply_max_delay budgets to 1 ps makes the check exit 1 with 7 violated groups covering EVERY class - both gray-pointer directions, both APB toggle bridges, PMU/IRQ, and both domain-wide fallbacks. A separate control tightening only the 0.5x/0.9x multipliers gave exit 1 with 4 groups. So the PASS is a real measurement, not an empty report.

title: ASAP7 resizer setup/hold slack margins are ~1000x too small (ns value vs ps liberty) - affects every ASAP7 signoff
description:
Same class as the known SDC units bug (Runs 7-32 ns-vs-ps), but for the RESIZER MARGINS, and still live in every ASAP7 config today.

MECHANISM (verified end to end):
1. librelane declares PL/GRT_RESIZER_{SETUP,HOLD}_SLACK_MARGIN with units="ns" (librelane/steps/openroad.py:2258-2261, 2327-2330).
2. The tcl passes the value RAW to OpenROAD: 'lappend hold_args -hold_margin $::env(PL_RESIZER_HOLD_SLACK_MARGIN)' (scripts/openroad/rsz_timing_postcts.tcl:45, rsz_timing_postgrt.tcl:48; same for -setup_margin at :35/:38).
3. OpenROAD/OpenSTA interpret those margins in the LIBERTY time unit. ASAP7 liberty is time_unit: "1ps" (asap7sc7p5t_SEQ_RVT_TT_nldm_220123.lib:45).
=> pnr/asap7/*/config.json values of 0.075 and 0.1 mean 0.075 ps and 0.1 ps, not 75 ps / 100 ps. Effectively ZERO guard band.

PROOF (GH #96 runs, SoC): run 17 used PL/GRT hold margin 0.075, run 18 used 0.030. Final netlists are BYTE-IDENTICAL (md5 5d6ca24b90497f115881dde6ae83c1b8 both), HB4xp67 hold-buffer count identical at 136 in runs 16/17/18, and per-clock timing identical to 6 decimals (cpu_clk WNS -44.927727, sys_clk +106.217033). A 2.5x change in a real margin cannot produce a bit-identical result; a change between two values that both round to ~0 ps does exactly that.

BLAST RADIUS: every ASAP7 run in this repo believed it had 100 ps setup / 75 ps hold guard band and actually had ~0. That includes the signed-off CPU (1282 MHz, RUN_2026-06-02_20-37-12), the GPU, and the Phase 5 SoC run-14 signoff (571 MHz). Their reported slacks are still REAL (STA is independent of the resizer margin) - what is missing is the extra optimisation guard band, so the designs sit closer to the cliff than the configs imply, and they are more exposed to OCV/derate than documented.

FIX: express these in ps for ASAP7, e.g. PL/GRT_RESIZER_SETUP_SLACK_MARGIN 100 and PL/GRT_RESIZER_HOLD_SLACK_MARGIN 75 (or whatever guard band is actually wanted). Do NOT blanket-apply to sky130/freepdk45 configs - those liberties are in ns, where the current values are already correct. Re-check each PDK's time_unit before editing. Expect area/power to grow once the margins become real.

Found while diagnosing GH #96 cpu_clk hold-buffer padding (bead claude_verilog_test-8nz).
close_reason: Config fix landed 2026-08-07 (5 ASAP7 configs, per-PDK time_unit verified first; sky130/freepdk45 correctly untouched). Re-sign-off under real margins now confirmed for the CPU macro (RUN_2026-08-09_14-05-02 at 20/10 ps) and the multiclock SoC (run 23 at 45/25 ps, both domains MET), which also retires the global-knob risk this bead flagged. Only the GPU macro still carries ~0 guard band; closing that is the ~2.5-day block run deliberately deferred under bead buw, so it is tracked there. See the residue-audit comment for the measurements.

comments.author: RD-Chuanseng.Ng
comments.text:
FIXED 2026-08-07. Liberty time_unit verified per PDK before editing: ASAP7 = 1ps (asap7sc7p5t_SEQ_RVT_TT_nldm_220123.lib:45), sky130 = 1ns, freepdk45 = 1ns. sky130/freepdk45 configs deliberately untouched and confirmed untouched (git diff --stat empty for both trees); freepdk45 has no resizer-margin keys at all and sky130's ns values were already correct.

  cpu/config.json            780 ps  -> setup 20 / hold 10 ps  (kept UNDER the achieved slack so the guard band cannot demand more than the design is known to reach)
  gpu/config.json           1750 ps  -> setup 45 / hold 25 ps
  template/config.json       705 ps  -> setup 20 / hold 10 ps
  soc/config_multiclock.json 1750 ps -> setup 45 / hold 25 ps
  soc/config.json            NUMERICALLY UNCHANGED (0.1/0.075) + documentation comment only -- this is the run-14 byte-reproducible M11 sign-off artifact, so the corrected values live in config_multiclock.json instead. Any new SoC PD work should use the multiclock config.

CARRIED RISK, flagged and not yet exercised: PL/GRT_RESIZER_*_SLACK_MARGIN is a single GLOBAL knob, not per-clock-domain. In config_multiclock.json the 45/25 ps values are sized off the 1750 ps sys_clk but also apply to the 780 ps cpu_clk domain, which as of run 19 is at -32.3 ps. A real margin on an already-failing domain may drive the resizer harder (plausibly helpful) or may fail to converge. Watch cpu_clk specifically on the next multiclock run.

Every prior ASAP7 sign-off (CPU 1282 MHz, GPU, SoC run 14) therefore ran with a ~0.075-0.15 ps guard band. Reported slacks remain valid; the guard band behind them does not.

comments.author: RD-Chuanseng.Ng
comments.text:
Two real findings from preflight (2026-08-05):

(1) OpenSTA SILENTLY DEGRADES an unbindable create_clock into a VIRTUAL clock. 'create_clock -name cpu_clk -period 780 [get_ports cpu_clk_i]' against a netlist with no cpu_clk_i port does NOT error - it yields a clock object that reports period=780 and would appear as a second 'Clock:' block in OpenROAD clock.rpt, while having is_virtual=1, 0 sources and 0 registers. Measured on the run-14 netlist: sys_clk is_virtual=0/sources=1/registers=43764 vs cpu_clk is_virtual=1/sources=0/registers=0. So 'clock.rpt shows two clocks' is NOT evidence of a real 2-domain run and would have green-lit a 5h run that timed nothing in the CPU domain. New gate: pnr/scripts/check_multiclock_sdc.tcl asserts is_virtual=0 + >=1 source pin + >0 registers per domain, emits MC-CHECK-RESULT: PASS|FAIL, exit 0/1/2. Validated as a NEGATIVE control against the run-14 netlist (exit 1, all 4 failure modes named).

(2) pnr/asap7/soc/runs was created as a REAL directory on / by a concurrent run before the symlink guard could fire. '[ -L runs ] || ln -sfn /nobackup/asap7_soc_runs runs' then nested the link as runs/asap7_soc_runs and the run still landed on / (7.4G free vs ~6G per full run). Two LibreLane runs were live at once on the 15GiB host; the redundant synth-only one was killed. Guard hardened: an existing non-symlink runs/ is now a hard error with migration instructions, verified to fire. MIGRATION STILL PENDING before any full run: mv pnr/asap7/soc/runs/RUN_* /nobackup/asap7_soc_runs/ && rm -rf pnr/asap7/soc/runs.

comments.text:
Gate B run 1 (RUN_2026-08-05_21-20-25) FAILED at 05-checker-yosysunmappedcells: '2 Unmapped Yosys instances found', exit 2. Root cause: sv2v resolves `ifdef ITSELF, before yosys runs, and the asap7-soc-sv2v target passed NO --define (unlike sky130-soc-sv2v). So USE_ICG_CELL from config.json VERILOG_DEFINES arrived too late -- rv32i_clock_gate.sv had already been frozen into its behavioural always_latch branch, which yosys infers as $_DLATCH_N_ and cannot map to any ASAP7 cell. Never bit before because the SoC had no clock gates until the PMU epic (#98) + #93 added u_cpu_cg/u_gpu_cg after the run-14 sign-off. Fix: SOC_SV2V_DEFINES := --define=USE_ICG_CELL in the asap7 sv2v recipe; regenerated netlist now instantiates ICGx1_ASAP7_75t_R (present in asap7sc7p5t_SEQ_RVT_TT liberty AND asap7sc7p5t_SIMPLE_RVT_1x.lef) with zero en_latch. Deliberately NOT adding __pnr__ (boot_rom.sv branches on it and run 14 was built without it -- adding it would change the PPA baseline; note sky130 DOES pass it, an inconsistency worth its own bead) nor SRAM_ASAP7 (no file in SOC_SV_FILES branches on it). sky130 must NOT get USE_ICG_CELL: ICGx1 is ASAP7-only and sky130 has real latch cells.

Also confirmed the 27 'used but has no driver' bits (cpu_bridge_s_{awlen,awsize,awburst,wlast,arlen,arsize,arburst}) are NOT a regression: run 14's pre_synth_chk.rpt has the identical 27 bits under the pre-CDC name cpu_m_*. Same pre-existing bead g0o condition the 571 MHz signoff already carried.

RUN 18 COMPLETE (RUN_2026-08-06_09-44-51, exit 0) = NULL RESULT, and the reason is a repo-wide bug.
Per-clock identical to run 17 to 6 decimals: sys_clk +106.217033 PASS / cpu_clk -44.927727, 162 violators, 1212.23 MHz. Final netlist md5 BYTE-IDENTICAL to run 17 (5d6ca24b90497f115881dde6ae83c1b8); HB4xp67 count 136 in runs 16, 17 AND 18.

title: APB3 debug port crosses into CPU domain unsynchronised (GH #95 gate finding)
description:
The GH #95 cdc_snitch gate's only unwaived residue: 233 registers, all one finding.

Top-level apb_* debug ports (apb_paddr_i/psel/penable/pwrite/pwdata) feed u_cpu
directly at soc_top.sv:825-832 with NO synchroniser. GH #93 moved u_cpu onto
cpu_gated_clk, so a chip-boundary bus silently migrated from the fabric domain
into the CPU domain. Affected regs: u_cpu.dbg_pc_wr_data[*], u_cpu.dbg_ctrl_reg[*],
u_cpu.dbg_reg_wr_en, u_cpu.halt_latch_q.

Pre-#93 the implied external contract was 'drive apb_* synchronously to clk_i'.
Post-#93 it silently became 'synchronously to cpu_clk_i'. Nothing documents this.
Multi-bit paddr/pwdata means the failure mode is not just metastability but
incoherent address/data capture.

Compounding: pnr/constraints/phase5_soc_multiclock.sdc:151-155 still asserts the
opposite -- 'the APB3 debug slave sits on apb_interconnect, entirely in the fabric
(sys_clk) domain'. Harmless for timing (line 169 set_false_paths the ports) but the
rationale is now wrong and will mislead.

Options: (a) bridge it with a second apb_cdc_bridge instance, s-face clk_i /
m-face cpu_gated_clk -- restores the pre-#93 contract and makes the SDC true again,
reuses verified IP, debug is an 'infrequent config path' so latency is irrelevant;
(b) declare apb_* a cpu_clk-domain port and fix the SDC rationale + document the
external contract; (c) accepted-risk waiver and defer.

Blocks the GH #95 BAD=0 gate from going green.

title: cocotb sim_build dirs exhaust the root FS during soc_all (results.xml write fails after tests PASS)
description:
MEASURED 2026-08-14 on branch fix/spi-miso-sync-a2g: soc_all aborted twice at the dma target with 'ERROR: results.xml was not written by the simulation!' AFTER all 6 dma tests reported PASS and Verilog $finish. Re-running the dma target standalone passes and writes results.xml (EXIT=0), so it is not an RTL or testbench fault -- it is intermittent ENOSPC.

ROOT CAUSE: root FS was at 99% (2.1 GB free) while tb/cocotb/soc holds 26 per-target sim_build dirs at ~192 MB each (~5 GB total). Per-target SIM_BUILD is correct and must stay (bead 7je fixed a real false-pass with it), but it multiplied the footprint ~26x. Any RTL edit invalidates all of them, so a full soc_all rebuild needs several GB the disk does not have; the run dies part-way, and the failure surfaces as a post-test results.xml write error rather than anything that looks like a disk problem.

WHY THIS MATTERS BEYOND ANNOYANCE: the failure mode prints per-suite PASS lines right up to the abort. A reader skimming the log sees PASS everywhere and a make error at the end -- easy to misread as flaky infra and re-run, which is exactly what happened here. It is also silent about the real cause.

WORKAROUND APPLIED 2026-08-14 (not a fix, not committed -- it is local filesystem state): all 26 dirs moved to /nobackup/claude_sim_build/soc/ and symlinked back from tb/cocotb/soc. Root went 2.1 GB -> 3.8 GB free. /nobackup has 502 GB.

REAL FIX: make the SIM_BUILD base configurable in tb/cocotb/soc/Makefile -- e.g. SIM_BUILD_ROOT ?= . with SIM_BUILD=$(SIM_BUILD_ROOT)/sim_build_$@... -- so a developer or CI can point it at scratch without symlink surgery. CLAUDE.md already documents routing SIM_BUILD to /nobackup for the AMS cosim flow; this generalises the same idea to the whole soc suite. Consider also a 'make clean-sim-builds' target and a pre-flight free-space check that fails loudly instead of dying mid-run.

title: Decide: refresh pnr/asap7/soc/macro/gpu_top.* + re-baseline SoC after GPU FP_PIN_ORDER_CFG lands
description:
GH #96 follow-up (claude_verilog_test-606): pnr/asap7/gpu/pin_order.cfg now pins the GPU macro's boundary side+order. Measured (RUN_2026-08-10_19-04-14, 24-odb-customioplacement/gpu_top.def vs checked-in pnr/asap7/soc/macro/gpu_top.lef): side+order match exactly (0/325 mismatches across N/E/S/W), but io_place distributes pins evenly along each edge while the checked-in LEF's spacing came from irregular free-floating placement -- so absolute coordinates differ on all 325 pins (median 42.6um, p90 ~117um, max 223.5um displacement on a 340x340um die). This is a ONE-TIME, order-preserving shift (unlike the CPU's 393/401 cross-edge reshuffle) that will happen on the *next* GPU macro regeneration under this cfg, then stay stable forever (same cfg -> identical output, by construction).

Decision needed: the checked-in pnr/asap7/soc/macro/gpu_top.{lef,lib,...} and the run-23 SoC sign-off baseline were built against the OLD (unpinned, irregular) GPU boundary. They were deliberately NOT refreshed as part of claude_verilog_test-606 (that bead was a determinism proof, not a macro refresh -- see pnr/asap7/gpu/README_pin_order.md 'What pinned actually guarantees'). Before the next GPU macro regeneration is folded into any SoC build, someone must: (1) regenerate pnr/asap7/soc/macro/gpu_top.{lef,lib,netlist} from the pinned config, (2) re-run the ASAP7 SoC multiclock flow against the new abstract, (3) re-verify sys_clk timing still closes (currently +74.8ps margin at run 23, i.e. not much headroom) given SoC-level placement around the macro will shift somewhat the same way u_cpu's did in GH #96 (though this shift is milder / order-preserving, not a full reshuffle).

comments.text:
INVESTIGATION 2026-08-11 — four measured findings that change the cost side of this decision.

1) THE AUG GPU RUN WAS KILLED, NOT FAILED. RUN_2026-08-10_19-04-14 died at step 37 openroad-repairdesignpostgrt with 'failed unexpectedly' + 460x GRT-0026. That step dir's mtime (09:35:01) is the SAME SECOND as the flow ERROR and the orchestrator's own abort note, so the error is the consequence of the SIGTERM, not an independent failure. Nothing about pin_order.cfg broke the run.

2) STEP 37 IS SUPPOSED TO TAKE ~20 HOURS ON THIS DESIGN. Commit b0dc46b documents repair_design_postgrt as the GPU runtime bottleneck at ~18.9 h (single-threaded GRT x2 + multi-thousand-iteration repair on ~485K instances, iteration count driven by the timing target, not die size). Measured on RUN_2026-05-28_06-29-48: step 36 finished 05-28 09:03, step 37 finished 05-29 05:55 = 20.9 h. The Aug run was killed ~7 h in — less than half way. The '7 h with zero log progress' that triggered the kill is NORMAL for this step.

3) A FULL GPU BLOCK RUN WITH POST-GRT REPAIR ON IS A ~2.5 DAY JOB, NOT A 4-5 h ONE. RUN_2026-05-28_06-29-48 spanned 05-28 06:29 -> 05-30 19:13; step 38 resizertimingpostgrt alone ran 05-29 05:55 -> 05-30 18:52 (~37 h). By contrast the 500 MHz signoff run RUN_2026-05-27_11-16-37 had post-GRT repair OFF and has no step 37 at all — it finished in ~3 h. That is the two-stage Run A / Run B pattern in PD memory.

4) A REGENERATION TODAY IS NOT A LIKE-FOR-LIKE REFRESH. Diffing resolved.json May-28 vs Aug-10, the GPU config changed in TWO ways, not one: FP_PIN_ORDER_CFG was added (intended), AND PL/GRT_RESIZER_{SETUP,HOLD}_SLACK_MARGIN went 0.1/0.075 -> 45/25, i.e. the bead s9f units fix that landed in e8b414f. The Aug run is the first GPU run ever with REAL margins. That is also the most likely reason step 37 was working harder than in May (10,444 slew violations, 3,044 buffers over 5,249 nets). So a regenerated macro is a NEW PPA point carrying two independent changes, not a boundary-only refresh — and the SoC re-baseline would have to attribute any delta between them.

ALSO CHECKED, no problem found: pnr/asap7/soc/macro/*.{lef,lib,nl.v.gz} are GITIGNORED copies (see that dir's .gitignore); the tracked source of truth is pnr/asap7/{cpu,gpu}/macro/. The two GPU LEFs differ in bytes (50.1K vs 56.3K, OBS/geometry) but place all 325 signal pins at IDENTICAL coordinates, so the documented 'cp gpu/macro/* soc/macro/' step is safe today and the pin_order.cfg derived from the soc copy matches the tracked abstract.

title: CPU macro APB read path: block-level SDC budget or register apb_prdata_o (root fix for the SoC cpu_clk exception)
description:
GH #96 run 16 found the SoC cpu_clk worst path is a single 800.71 ps COMBINATIONAL arc inside the rv32i_cpu_top macro: fabric FF -> u_cpu APB addr in -> arc -> u_cpu/apb_prdata_o[*] -> fabric FF. 33 of 194 cpu_clk violators are this class. #96 excepts it with set_false_path -through u_cpu/apb_prdata_o[*] (SDC section 10a), which is CONTRACT-CORRECT: the CPU's own standalone 780 ps signoff already does set_false_path -to [get_ports apb_prdata_o[*]] (pnr/asap7/cpu/constraints/asap7.sdc:121), so the macro was never characterized to meet 780 ps there. This bead is the ROOT fix that would remove the need for the exception.

WHY THE ARC IS SLOW: Liberty confirms apb_prdata_o[1] is direction:output timing_type:combinational with related_pin apb_paddr_i[9..11]/apb_psel_i/apb_pwrite_i -- a true feedthrough. Liberty emits topological arcs regardless of SDC exceptions, so the block false_path did not remove the arc, it only meant block P&R never optimized it. RTL cause: apb_prdata_o is a pure always_comb read mux (rtl/cpu/rv32i_cpu_top.sv:261-285), 10+ decoded addresses, 32 bits wide, sourced from CSR/PC/commit state spread across the block.

BUDGET (from run 16's failing path): arrival 1209.39 ps vs required 1004.05 ps => the arc must lose >=205.34 ps, i.e. be <=595 ps. SoC-side overhead measured on that path was ~79 ps before the macro (FF clk-to-Q 68.20 + INV 11.17) and ~55.7 ps after, i.e. ~10% of the period per side, NOT 40%.

TWO VARIANTS:
(A) Block SDC: replace the apb_prdata_o false_path with real set_input_delay/set_output_delay so block P&R is forced to close it, then regenerate macro views. Budget note: for a FEEDTHROUGH path the block budget is period - input_delay - output_delay, so both ends subtract. At 780 ps, 40%/40% leaves only 156 ps internal -- unreachable for this mux. ~80/105 ps leaves ~595 ps and matches the real SoC environment.
(B) RTL: register apb_prdata_o. One pipeline stage on an infrequent debug-read port collapses the arc to a clk-to-Q and REMOVES the combinational in->out arc from the .lib entirely, making variant A trivially satisfiable. APB tolerates the extra wait state (u_apb_dbg_cdc already waits on m_pready_i). Requires cocotb re-verification per the rerun-verification-after-rtl rule.

COST/SYNERGY: either variant needs a CPU block P&R re-run + macro-view regeneration + a SoC re-run. Regenerating the views is ALSO the fix for bead g0o (CPU macro abstract missing AXI4 burst ports awlen/wlast/arlen), so the two should be done together. Risk: adding a newly-timed path that the standalone signoff deliberately excluded may reduce the CPU's standalone 1282 MHz result.

NOT A #96 BLOCKER: after the -through exception the SoC limiter is the 161 non-macro violators at -44.93 ps, which are SoC-level logic and are untouched by any block-level change.
close_reason: FIXED via variant B (register the outputs), and it took all THREE APB outputs, not just prdata. apb_prdata_o, apb_pslverr_o and apb_pready_o in rtl/cpu/rv32i_cpu_top.sv are now pure registered outputs; the regenerated Liberty has no combinational arc on any output pin of the macro, so the SoC-side SDC 10a false_path -through u_cpu/apb_prdata_o[*] was RETIRED. Two intermediate attempts are recorded in the RTL so they are not retried: registering prdata alone merely RELOCATED the ~800 ps read mux into an 876.85 ps input SETUP requirement (run 20, cpu_clk -350.1 ps, all 15 violators ending at macro APB input pins), and a SETUP-phase decode for pslverr still left a 617.9 ps arc re-sourced from apb_psel_i. Every APB output pays ~600 ps crossing this block's internal distribution regardless of logic depth, so only a pure flop breaks it. External APB behaviour preserved: writes still complete in one ACCESS cycle (so psel&&penable&&pwrite write-commit pulses like dbg_pc_wr_en still fire exactly once), reads take one wait state. Merged in PR #135 (f7868b1); run 23 closed cpu_clk at +9.79 ps / 1282 MHz.

title: Tighten gray-pointer set_max_delay to 0.5x period; split post-route CDC SDC (OpenTitan precedent)
description:
Two SDC refinements with strong primary-source precedent, for GH #96 PD re-closure.
Item 2 may invalidate GH #94's CDC budgets entirely -- raised to P2 for that reason.

== 2. SET_MAX_DELAY MAY BE MASKED BY SET_CLOCK_GROUPS -ASYNCHRONOUS (potentially serious) ==

phase5_soc_multiclock.sdc has BOTH set_clock_groups -asynchronous (line 105) and
set_max_delay -datapath_only (sections 11-13) in ONE file. Its own comment at lines
100-103 asserts:

  'those get explicit set_max_delay -datapath_only overrides in sections 11-13 below,
   which OpenSTA honours even though the clock groups are otherwise asynchronous.'

That claim is UNVERIFIED -- per CLAUDE.md the SDC 'is not yet run through OpenSTA'.
And standard SDC exception precedence is:
    set_false_path  >  set_max_delay / set_min_delay  >  set_multicycle_path
set_clock_groups -asynchronous creates false paths between the groups. False path
wins. So the max_delay constraints are likely being silently DROPPED, which would
make all of GH #94's CDC budgets decorative.

OpenTitan hit exactly this and solved it by SPLITTING the SDC. Their check-only file
(hw/top_earlgrey/syn/chip_earlgrey_asic_check_only.sdc) opens verbatim:

  'These SDC's are not used for synthesis, since they collide with the current
   set_clock_groups -async constraints. Instead, they are used to time the design
   after P&R in order to make sure that the CDC crossings are all within spec.'

ACTION: run the SDC through OpenSTA and report whether the max_delay paths are timed
or dropped. If dropped, split into phase5_soc_multiclock.sdc (implementation, keeps
set_clock_groups) + phase5_soc_multiclock_check.sdc (post-route CDC verification,
keeps set_max_delay), per OpenTitan. Also fix the incorrect comment either way.

== 1. TWO-TIER CDC BUDGET ==

Current SDC bounds every CDC path to one destination-clock period. Precedent is
stricter and two-tier:
  OpenTitan check_only.sdc:  0.9 x destination period for all crossings,
                             GRAY_MAX_DELAY = 0.5 x period for FIFO gray pointers
  PULP cdc_fifo_gray.sv:     set_max_delay min(T_src, T_dst) -- the MINIMUM of the
                             two periods, not the destination's
Our mem_q read at ~1.0x is looser than OpenTitan's data path; our gray pointers at
~1.0x are 2x looser than theirs. Recommend 0.5x on the 10 gray-pointer crossings
(2 per FIFO x 5 FIFOs in u_cpu_axi_cdc) and 0.9x on mem_q.

PD/SDC change -> chip-design-pd:physical-design-orchestrator. Fold into GH #96.

title: Port OpenTitan prim_cdc_rand_delay metastability injection into cdc_2ff_sync
description:
Closes the 'metastability injection is not modelable in Verilator' residual gap
recorded in design_state.json:164 and CLAUDE.md.

OpenTitan does model it. hw/ip/prim_generic/rtl/prim_flop_2sync.sv wraps its first
synchroniser stage in:

    `ifdef SIMULATION
      prim_cdc_rand_delay #(.DataWidth(Width), .Enable(EnablePrimCdcRand))
      u_prim_cdc_rand_delay (.clk_i, .rst_ni, .src_data_i(d_i),
                             .prev_data_i(intq), .dst_data_o(d_o));
    `else
      always_comb d_o = d_i;
    `endif

prim_cdc_rand_delay.sv is 67 lines of plain RTL (randomised delay model, not #delay),
so it IS portable to a Verilator flow -- which contradicts our current claim that
metastability is unmodelable here. Defeatable per-instance via the Enable parameter.

Would give real coverage of the class of bug GH #93 found only by accident at a
divergent clock ratio. Apply to rtl/soc/cdc/cdc_2ff_sync.sv (every synchroniser in
the design is an instance of it, so one edit covers all 13+ crossings).

Verilator lint waiver precedent also in OpenTitan: hw/ip/prim/lint/prim_cdc_rand_delay.vlt
lint_off UNUSED for the whole file.

RTL change -> chip-design-rtl:rtl-design-orchestrator. Needs async_axi_fifo +
apb_cdc_bridge + soc_all re-run after.
notes:
IMPLEMENTATION LANDED BUT IS DEFECTIVE — reopened, do not close.

The infrastructure is right: rtl/soc/cdc/cdc_2ff_sync.sv now carries an optional
randomised-delay injector, guarded by `ifdef SIMULATION (defined only by
tb/cocotb/soc/Makefile, never by lint_soc / tools/cdc / pnr sv2v), parameter
RAND_CDC_DELAY_EN defaulting OFF, seeded for reproducibility. Verified: lint clean,
CDC gate 0 unwaived with counts BYTE-IDENTICAL to the pre-change baseline
(OK1 17791 / CDC 39 / OKX 330 / BAD 16088), so the synthesis path really is unchanged.

THE MODEL IS WRONG. hold_sel is redrawn only inside `always @(d_i)`:

    always @(d_i) begin ... hold_sel = ($urandom_range(0,99) < RAND_CDC_DELAY_PCT); end
    assign stage0_d = hold_sel ? sync_q[0] : d_i;

If hold_sel latches 1 on a d_i transition, stage0_d becomes sync_q[0] — a self-loop.
sync_q[0] then never changes, and because d_i has already finished transitioning the
always block never fires again, so hold_sel stays 1. The synchroniser is STUCK-AT its
old value permanently. That is not 'one extra cycle of settling delay', it is a
functional break of the primitive.

EMPIRICALLY CONFIRMED: forcing RAND_CDC_DELAY_EN=1 and running async_axi_fifo gives
TESTS=26 PASS=3 FAIL=23. The failures are the injector breaking the design, not the
injector finding design bugs.

This is why nothing in the repo opts in — the feature is dormant everywhere
(RAND_CDC_DELAY_EN=1 appears at zero instantiation sites), so as committed it delivers
exactly zero verification value while carrying the maintenance cost.

FIX NEEDED: redraw the hold decision once per DESTINATION CLOCK EDGE while
d_i != sync_q[0], not on d_i transitions. The natural form is to fold the decision into
the clocked stage-0 process (or an always @(posedge clk_i) helper), so a held cycle is
followed by another draw on the next edge and the value always converges. Compare
OpenTitan prim_cdc_rand_delay.sv, which takes both src_data_i AND prev_data_i and is
evaluated in the destination clock's process for exactly this reason.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA (none of which were met):
  1. With RAND_CDC_DELAY_EN=1 forced at every site, async_axi_fifo and apb_cdc_bridge
     must still PASS — a correct synchroniser must tolerate extra settling delay. Any
     failure there is a real finding to be reported, not the expected outcome.
  2. Demonstrate it CATCHES something: deliberately break a synchroniser (e.g. revert
     the 7a9f9d4 wr_ready_o reset gating) and show the suite fails with the injector on
     and passes with it off.
  3. Then wire at least one CDC-focused suite to run with it enabled, otherwise the
     feature stays dormant and buys nothing.
2026-08-13 NOTE CORRECTION — nothing is in the tree. The note above says 'IMPLEMENTATION LANDED BUT IS DEFECTIVE'; that is now historical. The defective injector was REVERTED in commit be485fd ('[RTL] bead rvs: revert the CDC delay injector, keep the finding') on branch feat/cdc-verification-gh95, which merged. Verified 2026-08-13: rtl/soc/cdc/cdc_2ff_sync.sv contains no RAND_CDC_DELAY / hold_sel / `ifdef SIMULATION text, and grep -r RAND_CDC_DELAY_EN over the repo returns zero hits. So there is no dormant feature and no maintenance cost carried today — this bead is a clean-slate REDO, not a repair. The defect analysis (hold_sel redrawn only inside always @(d_i) self-loops the synchroniser stuck-at, empirically 3 PASS / 23 FAIL on async_axi_fifo) and the three acceptance criteria below stand as the spec for that redo. Not scheduled this round (user decision 2026-08-13); ranked as the highest-value remaining verification item.

title: apb_cdc_bridge 2-phase toggle is not one-sided-reset safe; PMU resets CPU domain alone
description:
Research finding (primary sources) + empirical result from GH #95 directed testing.

== STATUS: no counterexample found in simulation; class concern remains open ==

GH #95 added 3 directed one-sided-reset tests to test_apb_cdc_bridge.py
(test_reset_asym_s_held_m_free, test_reset_asym_staggered_s_then_m,
test_reset_asym_staggered_m_then_s), on top of pre-existing
test_reset_mid_transaction_m_side / test_availability_* coverage. Suite is 22/22 PASS.

Verified clean across stagger windows of 1x/3x/8x the slower period, both release
orders, at 7/13ns, 18/4ns and 10ns-equal ratios:
  - m_psel/m_penable never pulse while m_rst_n_i is genuinely low (no fabricated
    destination write)
  - s_pready always force-completes within bounded time (no hang)
  - post-recovery reads/writes land exactly once (no duplication)

IMPORTANT: this is empirical absence-of-failure in the constructed scenarios, NOT a
proof that the class is safe. cocotb cannot establish the general property. A formal
treatment would need chip-design-formal (2-phase toggle FSM reachability under
arbitrary one-sided reset timing). Leaving this bead OPEN on that basis.

== THE UNDERLYING CLASS CONCERN (unchanged) ==

Both PULP and OpenTitan independently conclude a 2-phase (NRZ) handshake CDC is
unsafe under one-sided asynchronous reset, and both ship a 4-phase (RZ) variant
specifically to fix it:

- PULP cdc_reset_ctrlr.sv: 'We use a 4-phase rather than a 2-phase CDC to avoid the
  issues of one-sided async reset that might trigger spurious transactions.'
- OpenTitan prim_sync_reqack.sv: the RZ four-phase option 'is safe to reset either
  domain in isolation, since the two FSMs cannot get out of sync due to persistent
  EVEN/ODD states.' Its NRZ default instead carries the contract 'When resetting one
  domain, also the other domain needs to be reset with both resets being active at
  the same time', machine-checked by SyncReqAckRstSrc/Dst assertions.

rtl/soc/apb_cdc_bridge.sv is 2-phase toggle -- the variant both projects call unsafe.
Today largely masked by cross-coupled resets, BUT the PMU can reset the CPU domain
alone (pmu_cpu_rst_n), which is exactly the one-sided case.

Note apb_cdc_bridge.sv:281-335 documents a separate reviewed exception for
m_rst_n_s availability-gating -- different concern, not this one.

Resolution options if a counterexample is ever found: RZ 4-phase conversion (halves
throughput, irrelevant on a config path), or a documented+asserted contract that PMU
CPU-domain reset must not overlap an in-flight APB_PLL2 transaction.
notes:
ARM/open-source survey (GH #95) found a NAMED UPSTREAM FIX and confirms we are the minority choice.

Three independent implementations of an async APB bridge all use 4-phase RZ, not our
2-phase NRZ toggle, and at least one states the reason in exactly our terms:

  - ARM cmsdk_ahb_to_apb_async.v -- 4-phase, per its own OVL assertion names
    ('Test 4 phase hande shaking - phase 1', 'Req rising edge should only take place
    when Ack is low'). Structure otherwise identical to ours: 2x 2-FF on the handshake
    only, payload passed unsynchronised and held stable by the handshake.
  - Hazard3 hazard3_apb_async_bridge -- 4-phase.
  - OpenDAP bridge -- 4-phase, stating: 'A NRZI toggle handshake ... can cause spurious
    bus accesses when only one side of the link is reset.'

That last sentence is this bead, verbatim, from an upstream project.

So: our bridge's STRUCTURE matches ARM's async APB bridge exactly; only the handshake
ENCODING differs, and ours is the one all three projects avoided. Conversion to 4-phase
RZ halves throughput, which is irrelevant on a config path (APB_PLL2).

Note ARM's STA guidance for its async bridge is the older set_false_path on the payload;
our GH #94 set_max_delay -datapath_only is the stronger choice.
close_reason:
SHIPPED in PR #140 (merged, 10/10 CI checks). apb_cdc_bridge converted from 2-phase NRZ to 4-phase RZ, matching PULP/OpenTitan and all three surveyed async-APB bridges (ARM cmsdk, Hazard3, OpenDAP). The cheaper 'document a contract' option was rejected as unsound here: OpenTitan's NRZ contract requires the other domain to be reset too, overlapping, which PD_CPU power-down cannot honour, and the PMU has no drain/quiesce step.

Verified: sim lint clean; test_apb_cdc_bridge 23/23 including a NEW test_rz_four_phase_structural_proof that discriminates the encodings (the pre-existing 22 pass on BOTH, which is why GH #95's directed one-sided-reset testing never found a counterexample); soc_all 179/179 across 25 suites; CDC-filter non-vacuity gate PASS with negative control.

Caught during integration and worth remembering: the rename silently broke check_cdc_timing.tcl's filters (still matching *req_toggle_q*), which would have made the post-route CDC check examine zero nets -- bead 7l5's failure mode, re-introduced and nearly shipped. Also two review-caught doc contradictions the conversion itself introduced (fd11176).

RESIDUE, filed separately: set_max_delay -datapath_only BUDGET compliance is still unverified -- binding is proven, budgets are not, and that needs post-route delays from a full SoC run.

comments.author: RD-Chuanseng.Ng
comments.text:
VERIFIED + PR #140 opened on fix/apb-cdc-4phase-rfz (commit da73ac6).

RESULT: sim lint clean (0 errors, no apb_cdc_bridge warnings); test_apb_cdc_bridge 23/23; soc_all 179/179 across 25 suites, 0 failures. Note the baseline in this bead's history (159/159, 21 suites) is stale -- the suite count grew with the PMU/CDC/multiclock work. The divergent-ratio suites (soc_multiclock, soc_pll_multiclock at 7ns/3ns) are included and green.

NO testbench needed a latency update. Throughput on this path is intentionally halved by the RZ conversion, and nothing in the regression had hard-coded the old 2-phase cycle count, so the extra wait state passed through cleanly. axil_to_apb's tolerance of arbitrary pready wait states held in practice, not just on paper.

THE DISCRIMINATING TEST NOW EXISTS. test_rz_four_phase_structural_proof walks all four phases and asserts the RZ-defining ordering: req_q still 1 when ack_s asserts, ack_s still 1 when req_q falls, s_state_q visiting S_DROP. That sequence is impossible on the old NRZ encoding -- unlike the pre-existing 22 tests, which pass on BOTH encodings and therefore never proved anything about this bead. This is the artifact the bead was missing: the GH #95 one-sided-reset tests found no counterexample precisely because cocotb could not distinguish the encodings.

TWO DEFECTS CAUGHT DURING INTEGRATION, both worth recording:
1. The new test initially FAILED on correct RTL -- it compared s_state_q against 3 (S_DONE) while its own message said S_DROP (2); the enum is S_IDLE=0, S_REQ=1, S_DROP=2, S_DONE=3, and the TB documented that correctly elsewhere in the same file. Phases 1-3 (the real ordering proof) had passed. State ordinals are now named constants in the TB so a structural check cannot silently assert against the wrong one.
2. pnr/scripts/check_cdc_timing.tcl still filtered on *req_toggle_q* / *ack_toggle_q* for u_apb_pll2_cdc and u_apb_dbg_cdc. After the rename those match ZERO nets, so the post-route CDC budget check would have reported clean because it examined nothing -- bead 7l5's exact failure mode, re-introduced by this change and nearly shipped. Filters repointed at req_q/ack_q with a comment tying them to the rename.

CARRIED, NOT CLOSED BY THIS BEAD: the SDC edits are comment/line-number only (the set_max_delay exceptions target instance names u_req_sync/u_ack_sync/u_apb_pll2_cdc/u_apb_dbg_cdc, which did not change) and are Tcl-SYNTAX-validated only. Binding against a real netlist is unverified -- it needs a PD run, and the CDC budget check's non-vacuity on the new names has not been demonstrated by negative control the way 7l5's fix was.

'make librelane-asap7-soc-multiclock --to OpenROAD.STAPrePNR' ran 7h21m stuck in ABC at 10.2 GB RSS on a 15.9 GB host (2 GB available), against a 74-minute budget from run 23's step-04 timing, and had produced no netlist. title: Test live PMU power-cycle at a divergent cpu_clk/clk ratio (GH #90 residual)
description: Residual coverage gap identified while fixing bead 542. No suite exercises a LIVE, firmware-driven PMU power-cycle (runtime write to PMU CTRL, CPU domain off then on) while cpu_clk_i and clk_i run at different rates - which is exactly the scenario bead 542's bug lived in. Existing coverage validates the two halves separately: cold boot at a divergent ratio (soc_multiclock 4/4) and PMU sequencing at 1:1 (test_pmu 10/10, tb_pmu instantiates pmu.sv standalone with no CDC at all). The 542 fix (soc_top.sv commit 30beab3: cpu_gated_clk_en = ~pmu_cpu_clk_dis_sync & pmu_cpu_rst_n_cpu_sync) is justified structurally with unbounded skew tolerance, but is not directly tested. Suggested test: extend the soc_multiclock suite with a firmware sequence that powers the CPU domain down and back up via the PMU, asserting the CPU resumes with architectural state intact (PC/MSTATUS/MTVEC preserved - see docs/POWER_DOMAIN_EVALUATION.md:25, retention-by-construction because the behavioral model clock-gates rather than removing supply). Owner: verification-orchestrator.

title: PD port stubs missing cpu_clk_i/cpu_rst_n_i (blocks GH #96 multi-clock PD re-closure)
description: GH #92 added top-level ports cpu_clk_i/cpu_rst_n_i to soc_top and GH #93 made them load-bearing (u_cpu_cg is sourced from cpu_core_clk). title: pmu.sv power-up ordering unsafe across async CPU domain (GH #90 follow-up)
description: Found during GH #93. pmu.sv's per-domain sequencer asserts rst_n_w=1 (DOM_PU_RST) one full core_clk cycle BEFORE it asserts clk_en_w=1 (DOM_PU_CLK) on the power-up path. Since GH #93, pmu_cpu_rst_n and pmu_cpu_clk_en cross into the independently-clocked cpu_core_clk domain through two SEPARATE 2-stage synchronisers, so the 1-cycle offset is not structurally preserved downstream. A live firmware-driven CPU power-down/up cycle could see cpu_domain_rst_n release before the clock ungates - the same bug class as 4398c2e, narrower window. Cold boot is unaffected (verified: soc_all 159/159). Fix likely in pmu.sv: merge DOM_PU_RST/DOM_PU_CLK, or ungate the clock before releasing reset. Note the UPF fixes the sequencing order, so check phase5_soc.upf compliance before changing it. Untested area: no suite exercises PMU-driven live power-cycling across domains.
notes: Fixed in rtl/soc/soc_top.sv (not pmu.sv -- UPF-mandated ordering preserved). Gated u_cpu_cg enable with pmu_cpu_rst_n_cpu_sync: cpu_gated_clk_en = ~pmu_cpu_clk_dis_sync & pmu_cpu_rst_n_cpu_sync. Verified lint_soc 0 errors, make pmu 10/10, soc_boot 3/3 (100/100 stability), soc_multiclock 4/4. Commit on feat/cpu-domain-cdc-gh93.

title: Sky130 SoC Stage-2: setup fails at ss corner (WNS -8.9ns); sign-off gated to tt only
description:
Found 2026-07-28 auditing run RUN_2026-07-27_17-15-57. At 65 MHz (CLOCK_PERIOD 15.385 ns) the SoC closes setup at tt and ff but FAILS at all three ss corners: max_ss_100C_1v60 WNS -8.902 ns / TNS -118.16 ns; nom_ss -7.767; min_ss -6.386. Checker.SetupViolations reports 'No setup violations found' ONLY because pnr/sky130/soc/config.json sets TIMING_VIOLATION_CORNERS=['*tt*'] — STA_CORNERS runs all 9, but the gate ignores ss and ff. So the 'Stage-2 signed off at 65 MHz' claim is tt-only and should be stated that way.

ROOT CAUSE: the CPU hard macro's characterized clk->Q. Worst ss path is u_cpu/clk_i -> u_cpu/axi_araddr_o[15] = 8.155 ns, i.e. 53% of the 15.385 ns period consumed inside the macro before any SoC logic runs. The 12 worst ss paths are all u_cpu -> u_cpu or *_ -> u_cpu. This is bead 1ls (GH #123) resurfacing at the slow corner: 4.55 ns clk->Q at nom_tt, 7.54 at nom_ss, 8.12 at max_ss, against a 2.0 ns set_output_delay budget in pnr/sky130/cpu/constraints/sky130_cpu.sdc that gives the optimizer no pressure.

CONTEXT: 1ls was closed 2026-07-25 with 'Accepted 65 MHz (user decision)' after proving budget tightening is a dead end (8.0 ns budget failed to close Stage-1: WNS -2.950, 4826 hold endpoints). That decision was about not reaching 75 MHz — it did NOT establish that ss fails outright at 65 MHz. This bead records that distinct fact so it is not lost.

OPTIONS: (a) document the tt-only position explicitly and keep 65 MHz — cheapest, but then Sky130 Stage-2 is not a true multi-corner sign-off; (b) drop the SoC clock to ~41 MHz (1/(15.385+8.902)) so ss closes honestly; (c) re-harden the Stage-1 CPU macro against an ss-aware budget — 1ls suggests this is very hard for this topology. NOTE the ss numbers are honest for the CPU macro (9 per-corner CPU libs staged 2026-07-25, commit 86e89c1) but the SRAM macro is still TT-only analytical (bead o1i / GH #120), so the ss result carries some SRAM-model error. DECISION NEEDED — not PD tuning.
notes:
2026-07-29 RESULT — the 40 MHz relaxation did NOT close ss. RUN_2026-07-29_18-40-38 post-PnR STA at CLOCK_PERIOD 25.0 ns: max_ss setup WNS -4.328 ns (was -8.902 @15.385), nom_ss -2.885, min_ss -1.120. tt and ff clean.

WHY THE 41 MHz ESTIMATE WAS WRONG: it assumed path delay is invariant under relaxation. It is not. Effective path was 24.287 ns at T=15.385 and 29.328 ns at T=25.0 — 5.041 ns slower for 9.615 ns of relaxation, i.e. dpath/dT = 0.524. Each ns of period buys only ~0.48 ns of slack because the optimizer hands speed back (downsizes cells) as soon as it has margin. Linear two-point fit: slack = 0.476*T - 16.222, zero at T = 34.08 ns = 29.3 MHz. Crude extrapolation from two points — the same give-back effect may recur, so 29 MHz is a lower bound on the answer, not a guarantee.

PARKED. User decision 2026-07-29: fix the hold regression first (see 9t6/58q), then re-judge frequency against a clean baseline. CLOCK_PERIOD stays at 25.0 ns meanwhile. Do not chase ss further until hold is green at all 9 corners.
2026-08-13 DEFERRED (host-blocked). Already PARKED by user decision 2026-07-29 pending the hold regression; independently cannot be honestly closed before bead o1i (per-corner SRAM SPICE characterization, ~80-95 h), which is itself host-blocked. Removing from bd ready so the backlog stops offering unschedulable work; analysis retained verbatim.

title: Sky130 CPU Stage-1: RUN_POST_GRT_DESIGN_REPAIR is false — same unrepaired over-cap nets as the SoC had
description: pnr/sky130/cpu/config.json:102 has RUN_POST_GRT_DESIGN_REPAIR: false, the same setting that on the SoC (pnr/sky130/soc/config.json) left a 0.626 pF / 1.687 ns-slew net unrepaired and cost 1.03 ns on a macro clk->Q arc. Enabling it on the SoC (bead y7v, commit 1ef3426) recovered setup from -1.4304 to +1.3873 -- +1.15 ns better than the pre-existing baseline -- because it also repaired other over-cap/over-slew nets that had gone unrepaired for the whole Stage-2 history. The Stage-1 CPU hardening run has never had this step enabled, so rv32i_cpu_top's internal nets likely carry the same unrepaired slew/cap violations. Its .lib is not WRONG (arcs are characterized from the actual netlist) but is probably pessimistic, and the SoC consumes that .lib as a hard macro whose output drive cannot be resized. NOTE enabling it will likely hit the same RSZ-0090 abort if any macro .lib in the CPU flow declares an unachievable max_transition -- the SRAM fix was 8b11092. Also note the SoC antenna cost: pin violations went 144 -> 164 when this was enabled (bead 58q). Precedent: all ASAP7 configs run with this true.
notes: 2026-07-27 FINAL — RUN_2026-07-27_17-15-57 COMPLETE, adoption fully validated on every axis vs the previously published closure RUN_2026-07-26_16-05-43. TIMING, all three gated *tt* corners improved on BOTH setup and hold: setup nom_tt +1.3873->+1.8585 (+0.471), min_tt +2.5656->+2.8940 (+0.328), max_tt +0.3391->+0.8662 (+0.527); hold nom_tt +0.1444->+0.2932 (+0.149), min_tt +0.2489->+0.2919 (+0.043), max_tt +0.0923->+0.2706 (+0.178). Violator list EMPTY, and both Checker.SetupViolations and Checker.HoldViolations were LIVE GATES for this run. LVS 'Circuits match uniquely'. KLayout DRC 4 and Magic DRC 9081, both identical to baseline. ANTENNA IMPROVED 164->147 pin and 134->127 net -- I had predicted a regression there (design repair cost +20 pin at SoC and +4 at CPU previously); the better-repaired macro actually reduced it. max_tt, the tightest corner and the one where the CPU macro STILL violates setup internally at -0.12078, gained the most setup and nearly tripled hold margin, so that residual macro violation does not propagate to the SoC. CONCLUSION: the 0ro premise is confirmed end-to-end -- unrepaired over-cap/over-slew nets in the Stage-1 CPU made its .lib arcs pessimistic, and repairing them improves everything downstream. Macro views staged in commit 995c487, merged to main via PR #125.
close_reason: Validated by RUN_2026-07-27_17-15-57: staging the re-hardened CPU macro improved all three gated corners on both setup and hold (max_tt +0.527 setup / +0.178 hold), LVS match uniquely, DRC unchanged (KLayout 4 / Magic 9081), antenna improved 164->147 pin. Macro merged to main in PR #125.

title: Sky130 Stage-2: nom_tt hold violation -0.0923 ns at the sign-off corner
description: RUN_2026-07-25_13-29-40 shows nom_tt_025C_1v80 hold WNS -0.0923 ns / TNS -0.0923 (1 violating endpoint). The baseline (RUN_2026-07-24_21-36-12, nom_tt-wildcarded macro libs) reported nom_tt hold +0.1807 ns MET. The violation surfaced when the CPU macro moved to genuine per-corner Liberty views AND the antenna repair flow was enabled (2018 diodes, perturbing routing) -- the two changed together so the cause is not cleanly attributed. This is a violation at the ACTUAL SIGN-OFF CORNER, so it matters more than the ss-corner residuals. Note pnr/Makefile's librelane-sky130-soc recipe has --skip Checker.HoldViolations, so the flow does not gate on this. Investigate: identify the violating endpoint, confirm whether post-CTS/post-route hold repair ran and why it left this path, and whether it is diode-induced or lib-induced (a libs-only run would separate them).
notes: RUN_2026-07-26_16-05-43 CLOSES BOTH at nom_tt_025C_1v80: SETUP +1.38729 MET (was -1.4304), HOLD +0.14439 MET (was -0.0923 at baseline). Violator list EMPTY. Cleared OpenROAD.RepairDesignPostGRT with no RSZ-0090 recurrence. Step-40 setup recovered 3.0776 -> 4.0130 (baseline 4.0600). DIRECT PROOF the repair hit the real defect, not luck: u_cpu/axi_araddr_o[18] restored to fanout 1, cap 0.019504, clk->Q 4.544736 -- vs broken 2/0.625885/5.572786 and baseline 1/0.019349/4.544564. Setup is also +1.15 ns BETTER than baseline (+1.387 vs +0.2413) because post-GRT design repair fixed other over-cap/over-slew nets too. TWO fixes required, both committed: (1) clk_i excluded from set_driving_cell [all_inputs] and given its own clkbuf_16, worth +362 ps hold, setup-neutral, clock port 886->371 ps [e946350]; (2) RUN_POST_GRT_DESIGN_REPAIR true [1ef3426] + SRAM lib max_transition 0.04->0.5 [8b11092] to unblock the RSZ-0090 hard abort (40 ps unachievable in sky130_fd_sc_hd, PDK floor 43 ps; 0.04 was OpenRAM's characterization-range ceiling). GRT_RESIZER_HOLD_SLACK_MARGIN was investigated and EXONERATED (step-40 hold bit-identical at 0.15 and 0.05); left at default 0.05. DRC/LVS/antenna still pending -- run at step 52 of ~63. Do not close until those confirm.
close_reason: RESOLVED by RUN_2026-07-26_16-05-43: nom_tt_025C_1v80 setup +1.38729 (TNS 0.0) and hold +0.14439, both MET, violator list empty, LVS circuits match uniquely. Required two fixes: clk_i own clkbuf_16 driving cell (e946350) for hold, and RUN_POST_GRT_DESIGN_REPAIR true (1ef3426) + SRAM lib max_transition 0.04->0.5 (8b11092) for setup. Defect net u_cpu/axi_araddr_o[18] verified restored to baseline cap/clk->Q. Antenna regression 144->164 pin recorded on bead 58q.

title: SRAM_SKY130 hard-macro branch not covered by default regression
description:
tb/cocotb/soc/Makefile defaults SRAM_TARGET=freepdk45, and the soc_all target invokes sram_controller without SRAM_TARGET=sky130. So the OpenRAM hard-macro read path in rtl/soc/sram_controller.sv (rd_pend_q pipeline + 2-entry skid buffer handling the macro's 1-cycle registered read latency) is only exercised by a separate manual invocation.

Evidence: Stage-2 sign-off reported soc_all 99/99 AND sky130-branch 11/11 as two distinct runs, not one.

Risk: the SRAM_SKY130 branch can silently bit-rot on future unrelated RTL changes, since nothing in routine regression touches it. This is the branch that carried a P0 data-corruption bug (rvalid asserted one cycle before the macro's negedge-launched dout1 latched) found on 2026-07-24 - exactly the class of defect that must not regress unnoticed.

Fix options: add a soc_all_sky130 target, or make soc_all run the sram_controller suite twice (both SRAM_TARGET values), or add a CI job.
close_reason: Verified: tb/cocotb/soc/Makefile soc_all now runs sram_controller twice (default flat freepdk45 + SRAM_TARGET=sky130 OpenRAM macro branch). Full soc_all re-run: 18 suite invocations, 110/110 tests PASS, 0 FAIL, 0 SKIP, exit 0. sky130 sram_controller pass = 11/11, confirmed built with +define+SRAM_SKY130 -GMEM_WORDS=1024 and sim/sky130_sram_4kbyte_1rw1r_32x1024_8.sv (not a silent flat-array fallback). No ordering/stale-sim_build issue running sram_controller twice back-to-back. Log: /nobackup/soc_all_gh104/soc_all_68m_run1.log. design_state.json history[] + memory/verification/experiences.jsonl updated.

title: GH #104: sky130_sram_4kbyte_1rw1r_32x1024_8 has 4 KLayout DRC violations (upstream OpenRAM generator)
description:
Full-deck KLayout DRC (sky130A_mr.drc) on the Stage-2 SoC sign-off GDS (RUN_2026-07-24_09-58-19) found 4 real violations, all inside the OpenRAM-compiled sky130_sram_4kbyte_1rw1r_32x1024_8 macro's own internal cells. Confirmed via an isolation test (full KLayout deck on the macro's raw standalone GDS, no SoC context): identical violations, identical coordinates -- proving these are baked into the OpenRAM compile itself, not caused by or fixable via SoC-level PDN/floorplan/routing work.

Violations:
- m2.2 (met2 spacing <0.14um) x1, cell ..._wmask_dff, measured 0.055um (~60% short of spec)
- via2.2 (via2 spacing <0.2um) x2, cells macro-top + ..._bank, measured 0.125um (~37.5% short)
- m3.2 (met3 spacing <0.3um) x1, cell ..._bank, measured 0.29um (~3% short, ~1nm, plausibly grid-rounding but still non-conformant)

Root cause: the macro was compiled views-first with check_lvsdrc=False (OpenRAM's own DRC/LVS never ran), a deliberate choice made after the check_lvsdrc=True extraction died to a host reboot at ~7h. Confirmed these are in OpenRAM's generated assembly layer (compiler/modules/bank.py + the generic dff_array factory type used as wmask_dff), not a foundry-drawn primitive -- searched the installed sky130_fd_bd_sram primitive library, zero matches for these cell names.

USER DECISION (2026-07-24): accept + document for now, do not patch the GDS, do not retry OpenRAM config, do not attempt a DRC-clean regenerate at this time. Full record: pnr/sky130/soc/pdn.tcl (header comment) and memory/pd/run_state.md.

Follow-up: a future DRC-clean macro regeneration (options considered: (a) check_lvsdrc=True regen -- high non-completion risk given reboot cadence, and wouldn't fix anything by itself since OpenRAM geometry is deterministic, only reports; (b) OpenRAM config tweak, e.g. different words_per_row/column-mux, that might shift the bank/wmask_dff floorplan to avoid these spots -- speculative, ~190min+ per rebuild attempt; (c) targeted GDS patch of the 4 exact coordinates -- fast but fragile/non-reproducible from config).

Full-chip DRC signoff for GH #104 is NOT complete until this is resolved or explicitly re-accepted at tape-out-readiness review.
notes: Tracked on GitHub: https://github.com/chuanseng-ng/claude_verilog_test/issues/121
close_reason: Won't-fix, accepted with evidence (GH #121). efabless prebuilt sky130_sram_2kbyte_1rw1r_32x512_8 -- used in real MPW silicon -- ships 32 magic DRC errors in its own OpenRAM build log and is likewise analytical + nominal-corner-only; repo has no 4KB 32x1024_8 variant to swap to. Our 4 violations (one ~1nm) are OpenRAM generator norm, not a consequence of check_lvsdrc=False (geometry is deterministic; the checker only reports). All fix options cost 190min+/attempt on a host rebooting every 2-8h for no correctness gain. Re-open trigger: genuine tape-out-readiness review.

title: Sky130 Stage 2: CPU-macro + peripherals SoC, real DRC/LVS (GH #104)
design:
GH #104, part of epic #102 (bead n0i). Stage 2: pnr/sky130/soc/ — CPU as hard macro (Stage-1 native Sky130 views) + flat peripherals, NO GPU, real Magic DRC + KLayout DRC + Netgen LVS. Template = pnr/asap7/soc/ (adapt ASAP7->Sky130, drop GPU, flip DRC/LVS true).

APPROACH (PD-only; no functional RTL change):

title: PLL safety: clearing pll_enable (CONTROL[0]) self-bricks the SoC
description: CodeRabbit (PR #88) MAJOR, pre-existing (not introduced by the pll_subsystem refactor; same gating in old pll_axil_regs). pll_enable=CONTROL[0] in pll_apb_regs (clk_i domain, reset default=1). If firmware clears it: pll_rst_n=rst_n_i&pll_enable->0 -> PLL held in reset -> pll_locked->0 -> core_rst_n=rst_n_i&pll_locked->0 -> resets CPU+soc_bus. pll_apb_regs is NOT reset by core_rst_n (clk_i domain) so pll_enable stays 0 -> permanent deadlock; the APB master that wrote 0 is gone before it can write 1 back. FIX OPTIONS: (a) make CONTROL[0] set-only / non-clearable in SoC integration (firmware can enable, not disable); or (b) gate PLL reconfig so it doesn't drop core_rst_n in a non-recoverable way; or (c) add a startup/watchdog recovery. Functional design change -> own PR + soc_all re-verify. Natural to fold into #4 (3-PLL/CDC) where PLL control is reworked. NOT fixed in the refactor PR #88 (which preserved existing behavior).

CONSTRAINT-SIDE TWIN OF THIS BEAD (found 2026-08-06 while evaluating 40%/10% IO budgets for GH #96): pnr/asap7/cpu/constraints/asap7.sdc has ZERO references to the AXI4 burst-era ports. title: __pnr__ VERILOG_DEFINE is passed for the Sky130 SoC but not the ASAP7 SoC - the two flows elaborate different RTL
description:
Found during GH #96 Gate B while fixing the USE_ICG_CELL sv2v gap.

MEASURED: pnr/Makefile's sky130-soc-sv2v recipe passes __pnr__; the asap7-soc-sv2v recipe does not. rtl/soc/boot_rom.sv branches on `ifndef __pnr__, so the two PDK flows synthesise DIFFERENT boot ROM RTL from the same source tree.

LEFT ALONE ON PURPOSE during #96: run 14 (the accepted single-clock M11 ASAP7 signoff) was built WITHOUT __pnr__, and adding it would have changed the boot ROM contents and therefore the PPA baseline mid-campaign. That reasoning expires once a new ASAP7 SoC baseline is accepted.

RELATED GOTCHA worth keeping with this bead: sv2v resolves `ifdef ITSELF, before Yosys runs, so config.json VERILOG_DEFINES arrives too late for anything sv2v already decided. Defines that must reach the sv2v layer belong in SOC_SV2V_DEFINES in pnr/Makefile. That is what bit GH #96 Gate B - USE_ICG_CELL was in VERILOG_DEFINES only, so rv32i_clock_gate.sv was frozen into its behavioural always_latch branch and Yosys could not map the resulting \$_DLATCH_N_ (2 unmapped instances, exit 2). Note the converse: sky130 must NOT get USE_ICG_CELL - ICGx1_ASAP7_75t_R is ASAP7-only.

DECIDE: either pass __pnr__ on ASAP7 too (and re-baseline), or document why the ASAP7 flow deliberately elaborates the behavioural boot ROM.

title: SPI MISO sampled without 2-FF synchroniser (CDC hygiene)
description:
cdc_snitch (GH #95 gate) reports u_spi.rx_shift_q / u_spi.rx_push_data sampling the board-level asynchronous pin spi_miso_i directly into the fabric domain with no 2-FF synchroniser.

Benign in SPI *master* mode: the SoC generates SCLK, so MISO is sampled a known number of fabric cycles after the driving edge and is stable by construction. It is NOT clean by inspection though, and becomes a real metastability hazard in any future slave-mode or divided-SCLK use.

First reported by the 2026-06-09 cdc_snitch POC (docs/verification/CDC_SNITCH_POC.md:68-76), which recommended filing it. Carried in the GH #95 gate as an explicit kind:accepted-risk waiver (tools/cdc/cdc_config.yml, id spi-miso-unsynchronised-sample) rather than being silently canonicalized away.

Fix: instantiate cdc_2ff_sync on spi_miso_i in rtl/periph/spi_controller.sv, then drop the waiver. spi_controller.sv is Phase-5-verified RTL, so this needs a re-run of the spi suite (13 tests) + soc_all.
close_reason:
Fixed 2026-08-14 (PR pending). rtl/periph/spi_controller.sv now routes spi_miso_i through cdc_2ff_sync #(.WIDTH(1),.STAGES(2)) u_spi_miso_sync; the miso_in mux selects the synchronised bit in non-loopback mode (loopback path untouched). The kind:accepted-risk waiver spi-miso-unsynchronised-sample was DELETED from tools/cdc/cdc_config.yml, so the gate proves the fix rather than tolerating it.

EVIDENCE: CDC gate PASS with 0 unwaived / 71 waived and non-vacuous counts (OK1 17854 / CDC 40 / OKX 330 / BAD 16124 vs the pre-change baseline 17791/39/330/16088 -- the deltas are exactly the new synchroniser's registers). soc_all 183/183 across 26 suites, EXIT=0. Verilator lint 0 errors, warning set byte-identical to baseline.

test_real_miso_mode0 (the only non-loopback MISO test, CLK_DIV_EXT=7) PASSes with rx=0xC3 -- it compares the whole received byte, so an off-by-one bit shift from the 2-cycle sync latency would have corrupted it. Not a pass-for-the-wrong-reason.

KNOWN GAP recorded in the RTL comment, NOT silently retimed: with a REAL external slave, SPI_CLK_DIV==0 (half-period 1 clock) and ==1 (half-period 2 clocks) are no longer safe -- the 2-cycle sync latency meets or exceeds the half-period, so the sampled bit can be stale by a full bit position. No existing test drives a non-loopback slave at those dividers (loopback bypasses the synchroniser entirely at any divider), and the module's own guidance already recommends SPI_CLK_DIV>=7 for external slaves.

title: Sky130 CPU Stage-1: Magic DRC reports 27.7M li.3 violations — never passed, likely LEF-abstract artifact
description: Every Sky130 Stage-1 CPU run reports Magic DRC errors: 27733913 — BIT-IDENTICAL between RUN_2026-07-21_18-02-11 and RUN_2026-07-27_05-52-19, so it is systematic and deterministic, not caused by any recent change. KLayout DRC on the same runs is 0 and Netgen LVS says 'Circuits match uniquely', which makes the Magic result the odd one out. The report (*-magic-drc/reports/drc_violations.magic.rpt, 27.7M lines) is dominated by 'Local interconnect spacing < 0.17um (li.3)' with roughly a dozen other rule types present (licon.1, licon.5a, licon.8, licon.8a, poly.2/4/7/8, psd.10b, nwell.4). PRIME SUSPECT: pnr/sky130/cpu/config.json sets MAGIC_DRC_USE_GDS: false, so Magic runs DRC on the LEF/DEF-derived view where the sky130_sram_1kbyte_1rw1r_32x256_8 macro is an abstract black box rather than real GDS geometry — a classic source of spurious li spacing errors at macro boundaries. Worth testing MAGIC_DRC_USE_GDS: true on one run to confirm before treating any of these as real. CONSEQUENCE: Stage-1 CPU has never had a genuine Magic DRC sign-off, and that gap is inherited by everything consuming the rv32i_cpu_top macro.
notes: 2026-07-27 HYPOTHESIS REFUTED — RUN_2026-07-27_20-33-10 with MAGIC_DRC_USE_GDS=true. Magic DRC COUNT = 27,730,498 with REAL GDS vs 27,733,913 with the LEF abstract. Difference 3,415, about 0.01 percent — essentially IDENTICAL. The li.3 violations are NOT a macro-boundary/LEF-abstract artifact; they persist when Magic reads actual geometry. Same rule families in both reports (licon.1, licon.5a, licon.8a, poly.2/4/7/8, psd.10b). So Stage-1 CPU has a real, large, systematic DRC condition that needs its own root-cause, not a reporting artifact. IMPORTANT SCALE CORRECTION from the magic log: '[INFO] COUNT: 27730498' is followed by '[INFO] Should be divided by 3 or 4' — Magic counts each violation 3-4x, so distinct violations are roughly 6.9M-9.2M, still enormous. SECONDARY FINDING, and the reason the config was reverted: MAGIC_DRC_USE_GDS=true is NOT USABLE on this design. Magic hits fatal 'Unknown layer/datatype in boundary' errors reading the PDK SRAM macro's internal cells (sky130_fd_bd_sram__openram_dp_cell*, layers 235/0, 33/42, 33/43, 22/21, 22/22) and LibreLane aborts the whole flow with 'Encountered one or more fatal errors while running Magic'. The DRC itself completed and wrote its report BEFORE the abort, which is how we got the number. NOT an OOM — RAM went 11G->13G at death, no memory pressure; the magic-drc step ran 42 min (21:37->22:19). Config reverted to false so future CPU runs are not broken. NEXT STEPS if this is picked up: (a) sample actual li.3 coordinates to see whether they cluster inside the SRAM macro footprint or spread across the standard-cell array; (b) check whether the sky130A Magic tech file version matches what the PDK SRAM GDS expects, since the unknown layer/datatype errors suggest a tech-file/GDS mismatch that could also explain spurious li.3; (c) compare against the Sky130 SoC run, which reports only 9081 Magic DRC errors on a LARGER die — that asymmetry is a strong clue and worth explaining.
close_reason: RESOLVED — PDK SRAM macro artifact, WAIVED. Exhaustive streaming classification of all 27,730,498 coordinates in RUN_2026-07-27_20-33-10/63-magic-drc: 27,730,498/27,730,498 = 100.0000% lie inside the 10 sky130_sram_1kbyte_1rw1r_32x256_8 footprints; 0 in the routing channel, 0 in the standard-cell logic zone (max y = 907.87um; logic zone starts at 917.5um). All 26 rule families are 100% SRAM-internal — none leak outside; li.3 (922,628) is not even the dominant family (diff/tap.9 3.0M, licon.1 2.6M, li.1 2.3M). Reproduced independently twice with separate awk passes. SoC/CPU asymmetry explained: SoC declares the CPU as a hard MACROS entry with MAGIC_DRC_USE_GDS=false, so read_macro_lef loads the LEF abstract and Magic never touches SRAM-internal geometry — its 9,081 errors are a disjoint set (9,049 nwell.4 + 32 met4.4a), the already-documented DEF+LEF-abstract artifact class, not a diluted CPU flood. KLayout=0 on identical GDS because sky130A_mr.drc has explicit hierarchy-aware SRAM_EXCLUDE (select("-*sky130_sram_*kbyte_*") off nsdm/psdm/nwell, grouping the SRAM with I/O pad cells as a pre-verified macro) plus a working areaid:ce two-tier li1 scope — the relief Magic's COREID/coreli attempts but fails to deliver for this OpenRAM macro. Root cause: Magic's flat drc(full) engine cannot validate this dense custom OpenRAM macro's internals, independent of read path. Stage-1 sign-off stands on KLayout DRC=0 + Netgen LVS MATCH + DRT 0. Secondary techfile layer/datatype gap filed as y0w. Full write-up in memory/pd/run_state.md.

title: Sky130 Stage-2: antenna residual 154 pin / 129 net after repair (manufacturability FAILED)
description: After enabling the antenna flow (commit 86e89c1), RUN_2026-07-25_13-29-40 improved antenna from 556 pin / 440 net pre-repair to 154 pin / 129 net post-repair via 2018 inserted diodes (~72% reduction), but manufacturability.rpt still reports 'Antenna: Failed'. notes:
2026-07-31 RUN 5 (RUN_2026-07-31_05-13-54, HEURISTIC_ANTENNA_THRESHOLD=800) — VOLUME MODEL FALSIFIED. FINAL MECHANISM ESTABLISHED.

Cell count landed almost exactly as predicted (234,371 vs ~234k) but latency did NOT follow: 1.381585 ns, essentially identical to the 44k-diode runs, not the predicted 0.93-1.0. Hold failed at the same 5 corners (nom_tt -0.1623, nom_ss -0.1748, max_tt -0.4093, max_ss -0.5278, max_ff -0.0914). Antenna post-DRT 90/84, routing DRC 0, LVS PASSED.

THE ACTUAL MECHANISM — latency is BINARY on whether Odb.HeuristicDiodeInsertion runs at all:
    run        heuristic  stdcells   clk_i->u_cpu/clk_i   hold
    baseline      off     226,454        0.870159        clean 9
    run 3         off     226,952        0.933178        clean 9
    run 5         ON      234,371        1.381585        fails 5
    run 4         ON      270,217        1.410208        fails 5
    run 2         ON      272,003        1.388234        fails 5
    run 1         ON      271,858        1.439363        fails 5
Among the ON runs cell count spans 234k-272k (38k spread) with no material latency effect (1.38-1.44). Off: 0.87-0.93. Cell VOLUME is not the variable; the step RUNNING is.

WHY: the step wraps 1-odb-fuzzydiodeplacement -> 2-openroad-detailedplacement -> 3-openroad-globalrouting. It re-legalizes placement and re-routes globally after insertion. That perturbation costs ~0.45-0.5 ns at the clock root regardless of whether it inserted 7,970 or 44,742 diodes. Verified: both run 4 and run 5 show the same three sub-steps.

CONSEQUENCE — the trade-off is binary and NOT tunable. Three levers all failed for the same reason (they reduce WHAT is inserted; the cost comes from the pass RUNNING): DIODE_ON_PORTS off (run 2, no effect); clock-net exclusion patch (run 4, zero clock diodes, no effect); threshold 800 / 5.6x fewer diodes (run 5, no effect).

Keep a falsifiable guard on any future claim on this bead.

    run 3    140/120    clean 9       PASS      0
    run 5     90/84     fails 5       PASS      0
    run 4     40/39     fails 5       PASS      0
